_comment: TRY IT IN THE REAL APP — the one slide whose question is whether the thing WORKS, not how it looks.

Every other slide shows a picture, a recording, or a pane of the renderer against a fake backend: real to look at and touch, but no model answering and nothing saved to disk. This slide is for the rows of the contract marked `live-app` — the ones that say the feature actually does the thing.

It opens the window FOR him: served, the card shows an "Open the dev window" button beside the command. Opened as a plain file there is no server to ask, so only the command shows. Either way the window is a SEPARATE dev app alongside Destin's own; never tell him to poke his own running copy.
No pictures, so this deck names no images folder and no runs.
title: Saved searches — does it actually work?
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His answers are saved under it.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_stage: stage (optional): a try-it slide is what a `review` stage accepts.

steps._comment: One thing to do, one verdict. Two things to try are two slides, so each gets its own answer.
steps._comment_words: words: true — a try-it slide has no picture of its own; the app is in another window.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this point. It labels his answer.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The search box at the top of the session list
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there once the window is open.
steps.headline: Save a search, close the window, reopen it — is the search still there?
steps._comment_headline: headline: the one thing to DO, and the thing it proves. 25 words at most, no code words.

dev._comment: dev: where the window comes from. `serve` does not launch it — the card prints this line and he (or you, after telling him) runs it.
dev._comment_worktree: worktree: the checkout the window runs — a worktree name or a branch name.
dev.label: Saved searches
dev._comment_label: label (optional): the window title, so two dev windows are tellable apart in Alt-Tab. Defaults to the worktree name.
dev._comment_offset: offset (optional): only when a dev instance is ALREADY running — a second one needs its own ports.
dev._comment_profile: profile (optional): pair it with offset. Two instances sharing a profile share their state and fight.

steps.changed: The window runs the branch end to end — a real model answering, real files on disk, and the saved search written to your own settings.
steps._comment_changed: changed: what this window actually is, so he knows what he is testing.
steps.notice: A search you saved before closing is at the top of the list when the window comes back.
steps._comment_notice: notice: what to watch for. This is the thing his answer is about.
steps.risk: It is a second window on your desktop; close it when you are done.
steps._comment_risk: risk: the Risk card. The window itself is usually the risk worth naming.
steps._comment_yes: yes / no (optional): these are the defaults; relabel only when the verdict is not pass/fail.
